item.title: Upgrading and Installing Fedora 18 in VMware Fusion
item.description: I was thoroughly excited about Fedora 18 until I actually went to install it. I use Fedora 17 on a laptop and a desktop, but I also have copies in virtual machines that I use for testing – these virtual machines run in VMware Fusion on my Mac Pro. So never having used Fedora 18 during any of the betas or anything, first thing I did was try to install it in VMware.

item.title: Converting a VMware Fusion virtual machine to KVM
item.description: I’ve been running an instance of my Nagios XI monitor in a VMware Fusion virtual machine on my (aging) Mac Pro. The other day I found a blog post on How I converted a VMware VM to KVM and since my new LAN server is a beefy 8-core AMD FX-8120 with 32GB RAM (as opposed to the 2 x 2.66GHz dual-core Xeon with 16GB RAM that is my 5(?) year old Mac Pro), I decided to try moving the VMware Fusion VM to running on my Linux server (Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 with KVM).
